newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss to send new team to U.N. commission in Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Swiss to send new team to U.N. commission in Iraq.

text.p: Switzerland is to send a fresh team of soldiers to provide logistics support for the U.N. commission in Iraq overseeing the dismantling of Baghdad's weapons of mass destruction, the government said on Friday.
The departure of the unarmed five-man team on Sunday marks the 28th time Swiss soldiers have supported the U.N. Special Commission on Iraq (UNSCOM), the Defence Ministry said.
"Foreign missions of this kind are a sensible opportunity for Switzerland to offer its good services to the U.N. and thus the community of nations," a ministry statement said.

In a 1993 referendum, Swiss voters banned the government from sending armed peacekeepers abroad. But Switzerland has sent unarmed soldiers to back U.N. missions, and has lent UNSCOM its expertise in detecting chemical and biological agents.
